statement: A point $A(0,1)$ and a point $B(3,2)$ lie on the same side of the $x$-axis. A light ray travels from $A$ to a point $P=(x,0)$ on the $x$-axis and then to $B$. Find $x$ that minimises the total path length $AP+PB$.
solution:
The path length is $L(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}+1}+\sqrt{(x-3)^{2}+4}$. Differentiating, $L'(x)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}+\frac{x-3}{\sqrt{(x-3)^{2}+4}}$. Setting $L'(x)=0$ gives $\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}=-\frac{x-3}{\sqrt{(x-3)^{2}+4}}$. Squaring and solving yields $x=1$. (This is the classic reflection condition; the minimum occurs at $x=1$.)

hints: Write the total length as a function of x.
Differentiate and set the derivative to zero.
Solve the resulting equation (reflect B across the axis to check).
